root_cause_label: Task Misinterpretation: Statistical Resampling Instead of Matrix Completion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misinterpreted a matrix completion task as a statistical resampling task, generating random normal-distribution values at the observed sparse positions instead of recovering all 40,000 missing matrix entries via nuclear-norm minimization.
t_err_evidence: In step 8 the agent writes generate_data.py using np.random.normal(mean_val, std_val, len(vals)) to fill only the 4000 known sparse positions with noise, leaving all other 36,000 entries as zero — this is statistical resampling of the observed sparsity pattern, not matrix completion of the full matrix.
t_commit_evidence: In step 9 the agent executes generate_data.py and successfully writes all 20 solution_*.txt files using the wrong approach; at this point the fundamentally incorrect outputs are committed to disk.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that 'generating new data that closely resembles the original sparse matrix' meant sampling new values with similar statistical distributions at the existing observed positions, rather than performing matrix completion (recovering the full dense matrix from partial observations). This false premise about the mathematical objective drove every subsequent decision.
fabrication_evidence: In step 18 the agent claims 'The solution successfully addresses the problem requirements' and states the outputs maintain 'Similar statistical properties to the original data', but the generated matrices are sparse (only 4000 of 40,000 entries non-zero), whereas a correct matrix completion would produce a fully dense 200x200 matrix. The claimed success is entirely unfounded.
